bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 4 Crash State: DataValue_clear clear_noInit DataValue_clear
bug_description.normalized: The fuzz input sets the custom test allocator limit to 984 bytes and decodes as a top-level UA_DataValue whose value is a nested array-of-DataValue structure. During UA_copy, a deep copy of an inner Variant allocates a new DataValue array but then fails on a later arrayDimensions allocation. DataValue_copy handles that failure by clearing the partially copied destination. Variant_clear frees the just-allocated p->data array but, in the vulnerable version, leaves p->data unchanged. UA_copy then clears the same destination again on its own error path, and the second Variant_clear walks the already freed DataValue array, causing the observed heap-use-after-free read.

source.description: After the top-level DataValue encoding mask indicates that a value is present, the decoder materializes the attacker-controlled UA_Variant that later becomes the stale-pointer cleanup target.
source.value_from: The PoC bytes after the 2-byte little-endian type selector `0x0016` (`UA_TYPES_DATAVALUE`) and before the 4-byte allocator-limit trailer; the top-level DataValue encoding mask byte is `0x01`, so the remaining attacker-controlled payload is decoded into `dst->value`.

sink.description: Second cleanup of the same partially copied DataValue re-enters Variant_clear on a stale `p->data` pointer. The very first read of `p->storageType` comes from the first element of an already freed 192-byte UA_DataValue array, triggering the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ 4.

root_cause.description: Error cleanup frees `p->data` but does not clear the field afterwards. The fix adds `p->data = NULL;` immediately after `UA_Array_delete`, so the later `UA_clear` on the same destination no longer reuses a freed array pointer.

parser_admitted.description: After the harness dispatches `typeIndex == UA_TYPES_DATAVALUE`, project-side decoding enters `DataValue_decodeBinary` for the remaining payload bytes.

tainted_value_origin.description: The last four PoC bytes are interpreted as a little-endian uint32 and set the fuzz-only allocator limit. In the witness, `d8 03 00 00` becomes `memoryLimit = 984`, which is the low-memory condition required for the inner copy to fail after allocating its nested array.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness uses the last four PoC bytes as the custom allocator limit and the first two bytes as a type selector, then routes the remaining payload into `UA_decodeBinary` and `UA_copy` for a top-level `UA_DataValue`.

Decoding materializes a top-level `UA_DataValue` whose `value` is a `UA_Variant` array of two `UA_DataValue` elements; the second element itself contains another `UA_Variant` array of two `UA_DataValue` elements plus copied `arrayDimensions` state.

Deep-copying that nested structure allocates new DataValue arrays, then hits the 984-byte allocator limit when duplicating an inner `arrayDimensions` array, so the copy returns an error after a fresh nested `dst->value.data` array has already been allocated.

Error cleanup frees the newly allocated inner `dst->value.data` array without nulling the field. `UA_copy` then clears the same destination again, and the second `Variant_clear` reads through the freed DataValue array, producing the reported heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.note: The harness splits the attacker buffer into two roles: the last four bytes are reserved for the custom allocator limit, and the preceding bytes are forwarded to `tortureEncoding()` as the binary payload to decode and then copy.
The PoC trailer `d8 03 00 00` sets `memoryLimit = 984`. All later `UA_malloc`/`UA_calloc` requests on this path are checked against that attacker-controlled limit.

The first two payload bytes are `16 00`, so `typeIndex = 22` (`UA_TYPES_DATAVALUE`). Line 33 then dispatches the remaining payload into `UA_decodeBinary(..., &UA_TYPES[typeIndex], ...)` as a top-level `UA_DataValue`.
The top-level DataValue encoding mask byte is `0x01`, so `hasValue` is set and the attacker-controlled `UA_Variant` payload is decoded into `dst->value`.

The top-level Variant encoding byte is `0xD7`: array bit set, dimensions bit set, and type bits selecting `UA_TYPES_DATAVALUE`. `Array_decodeBinary` therefore reads `signed_length = 2`, allocates a two-element `UA_DataValue` array in `dst->data`, and later decodes one `arrayDimensions` entry for that top-level variant.

For the top-level element at index 1, its `value` decodes from another `0xD7` Variant header into a nested array of two `UA_DataValue` elements, again with one `arrayDimensions` entry. This nested array is the heap object that later becomes stale.

fine_trace.code: if(signed_length <= 0) { *out_length = 0; if(signed_length < 0) *dst = NULL; else *dst = UA_EMPTY_ARRAY_SENTINEL; return UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD; }
fine_trace.note: Inside that nested array, subelement 0's own Variant length field is negative (`0xFF202020` as `i32`), so the decoder stores `data = NULL` and `arrayLength = 0` for that subelement's `value`. The same subelement still carries one decoded `arrayDimensions` entry, so copying it later requires a 4-byte dimensions allocation even though its `data` pointer is NULL.
Decoding succeeded, so the harness deep-copies the top-level `UA_DataValue`. The crash happens during this `UA_copy`, not during the initial decode.

The top-level `DataValue_copy` reaches `Variant_copy` for `dstCopy->value` and allocates a fresh two-element `UA_DataValue` array for `dst->data`. It then starts copying the two top-level elements into that new array.

While copying top-level element 1, its inner `Variant_copy` allocates a fresh two-element `UA_DataValue` array for that element's `dst->value.data`. Copying subelement 0 then succeeds because only its single `arrayDimensions` entry must be duplicated. This leaves the next 4-byte allocation in the same inner copy as the first request that can exceed the 984-byte limit.

The next request is the inner `Variant_copy` at `src/ua_types.c:428` trying to allocate the outer element 1 `arrayDimensions` array (`num = 1`, `size = 4`). Because step 10 already consumed the remaining headroom, this predicate becomes true and the allocator returns NULL, so `UA_Array_copy` fails with `UA_STATUSCODE_BADOUTOFMEMORY`.

The failed inner `DataValue_copy` executes its error cleanup (`if(retval != UA_STATUSCODE_GOOD) DataValue_clear(dst, NULL);`). `Variant_clear` frees the just-allocated inner `dst->value.data` array from step 10, but the vulnerable code leaves `p->data` pointing to that freed array because no `p->data = NULL;` follows.

The same inner `UA_copy` that was copying top-level element 1 sees the non-GOOD return and clears that partially copied destination again. This second clear reuses the stale `dst->value.data` pointer left behind by step 12.

Second entry into `Variant_clear` on the stale inner `dst->value.data` pointer. `UA_Array_delete` walks the already freed two-element `UA_DataValue` array, and the first element read of `p->storageType` hits freed memory. ASAN reports the read at `0x610000000350`, 16 bytes inside the freed 192-byte region allocated at `UA_Array_copy:1061` and freed at step 12.

format.name: open62541 fuzz_binary_decode DataValue payload
format.contract: A 63-byte `fuzz_binary_decode` input whose first two bytes are little-endian `0x0016` (`UA_TYPES_DATAVALUE`), whose last four bytes are little-endian `0x000003d8` (custom allocator limit 984), and whose remaining bytes encode this exact nested shape: top-level `UA_DataValue` with `encodingMask = 0x01`; top-level `UA_Variant` with `encodingByte = 0xD7` (DataValue array with dimensions) and array length 2; outer element 1 also has `encodingMask = 0x01` and `encodingByte = 0xD7` with array length 2; the first subelement of that nested array has a negative Variant length so its `data` becomes NULL but it still has one `arrayDimensions` entry. This exact layout makes the inner `arrayDimensions` copy be the first allocation that exceeds the 984-byte limit after a fresh 192-byte nested `dst->value.data` array has already been allocated, exposing the stale-pointer double-clear in `Variant_clear`.
